https://www.flickeringmyth.com/the-girl-.text: Stieg Larson’s acclaimed mystery thriller The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is getting a new adaptation in the form of a series from Sky with David Oyelowo ( Silo ) and Viola Prettejohn ( The Crown ) in the lead roles. First published in Sweden in 2005 and then translated in 2008, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is the first novel in the Millennium Trilogy which follows Lisbeth Salander and journalist Mikael Blomkvist as they investigate a cold case of a wealthy family’s missing and presumed dead member. The book became a worldwide bestseller and launched a trilogy of Millennium films featuring Noomi Rapace as Lisbeth and Michael Nyqvist as Mikael. Dragon Tattoo was remade in 2011 by David Fincher with Rooney Mara and Daniel Craig in the lead roles. The new TV series will see Oyelowo as Mikael and Prettejohn as Lisbeth. The series will be brought to the modern day and expand on elements the feature films could not fit in, such as the extended Vanger family as Mikael and Lisbeth delve into the family’s long history and their complex relationships. The official synopsis reads: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo follows canceled star journalist Mikael Blomkvist and uncompromising hacker Lisbeth Salander as they investigate the disappearance of Harriet Vanger, who vanished more than three decades ago from the secluded island home of one of Sweden’s most powerful industrial dynasties. As they delve deeper into the Vanger family’s buried past, their investigation draws them closer to a chilling threat unfolding dangerously close to them in the present. The series is created by Amanda Coe, Steve Lightfoot and Angela LaManna, who will write and executive produce. Directing the series will be Reinaldo Marcus Green, who will also executive produce, Andrea Harkin and Amy Neil. Sony Pictures Television and Left Bank Pictures are producing. “Salander and Blomkvist are two of modern fiction’s most iconic and compelling characters, and we’re thrilled to have Viola and David bringing them to life for a new generation,” said Sky’s head of scripted originals Meghan Lyvers. “ The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo is an iconic story with themes of power, corruption, justice and violence against women that feel even more timely today,” said Left Banks’ Charlotte Moore. “In Viola Prettejohn and David Oyelowo, we have two extraordinary actors at the heart of this adaptation and really look forward to audiences enjoying their take on these compelling and complex characters.” Additional casting is to be announced in the coming weeks as production readies to begin in Lithuania next month. About Ricky Church Ricky Church is a Canadian screenwriter whose hobbies include making stop-motion animation on his YouTube channel Tricky Entertainment. Photograph: Rogelio V Solis/AP View image in fullscreen Curtis Flowers exits the Winston-Choctaw regional correctional facility with his sister Priscilla Ward in Louisville, Mississippi, in December 2019. Photograph: Rogelio V Solis/AP Mississippi Curtis Flowers, US man wrongfully imprisoned for 22 years, dies aged 56 Flowers, tried six times over 1996 murders of four people, faced execution before supreme court tossed his conviction Associated Press Thu 8 Oct 2026 18.36 EDT Last modified on Thu 8 Oct 2026 18.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Curtis Flowers, a Black man who spent more than 22 years in prison and was on death row in Mississippi before the US supreme court threw out his conviction and death sentence, has died. He was 56. Flowers’ family confirmed that he died on Wednesday at his home in Mississippi , attorney Rob McDuff told the Associated Press on Thursday. No cause of death was given, said McDuff, who was part of Flowers’ legal team. Flowers was 26 when he was arrested several months after the July 1996 shooting deaths of four people inside a furniture store in Winona, Mississippi . Curtis Flowers’ conviction overturned over removal of black jurors Read more At the time, prosecutors described him as a disgruntled former employee who sought revenge against the store’s owner because she fired him and withheld most of his pay to cover the cost of merchandise he damaged. Nearly $300 was found missing after the killings. Flowers was tried in the killings six times . Justice Brett Kavanaugh wrote in the high court’s 7-2 decision in 2019 that the removal of Black prospective jurors deprived Flowers of a fair trial. During the sixth trial in 2010, Flowers was sentenced to death. There were 11 white jurors and one Black juror who considered the case after district attorney Doug Evans struck five Black prospective jurors. Flowers remained in prison for six months after the supreme court ruling because he was still under indictment. He finally was released in December 2019 after a judge set bond. Mississippi dropped charges against Flowers in September 2020. “Today, I am finally free from the injustice that left me locked in a box for nearly 23 years,” Flowers said in a statement. “I’ve been asked if I ever thought this day would come. I have been blessed with a family that never gave up on me and with them by my side, I knew it would.” Explore more on these topics Mississippi US justice system Capital punishment US crime US supreme court US prisons news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed US news US politics Midterms 2026 World Climate crisis Middle East Ukraine US immigration Soccer Business Environment Tech Science Newsletters The Filter Wellness

https://www.yorkpress.co.uk/news/2659029.text: Charity Leisure Man who had a heart attack on stag do raises funds Charity Leisure By Karen Darley Reporter Share 0 Comments Jamie Miller with his partner girlfriend Jade Carlisle This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald. A MAN who had a heart attack after 'disappearing' on a stag weekend is raising funds for the hospital which helped save his life.. Jamie Miller, was part of a group of 16 on a trip to Newcastle, when he went missing. After a night out, he began a Friday morning with his friends with breakfast at the Mile Castle in Newcastle city centre. However he became separated from the group, crossed the road, and collapsed in a cemetery opposite the pub. Thankfully, a good Samaritan saw him collapse and was able to provide life-saving help. Jamie, who was then 37, said: " I was on a stag do in Newcastle. We had been out on the Thursday while the Euros were on. We had had a fairly normal night - we weren't going wild, we were due to fly to Poland the next day. "I woke up on the Friday morning and actually felt okay. We left the hotel at about quarter past nine, and that's my last memory. "But from what I have picked up, we walked into the town centre and into Wetherspoons. I walked out - and the rest of the group just assumed I was hungover, but I had collapsed in the churchyard opposite the pub. A member of the public must have seen this happen. "They found me and carried out CPR, got the defibrillator and called the ambulance. All the while my mates were still in Wetherspoons - not knowing what had happened. "I woke up in the Freeman Hospital not knowing where I was or what had happened." Jamie, from Terrington, said had it not been for the mystery stranger - and the paramedics and Freeman Hospital team who "did an amazing job," he probably wouldn't be here. "The staff said that I has been left for just five minutes more I would have passed away." Jamie's recovery has continued and while he missed the Polish leg of the stag do, he made it to the wedding over the summer. "Two years on, I'm now has fit as ever. I'm on medication for the rest of his life, but that�s a small price to pay." Following the incident, Jamie and his partner Jade, aimed to return to Newcastle to run the Great North Run in aid of the Freeman Hospital. "We were originally planning on completing it in 2025 but overlooked that fact that the Cardiologist would need to approve it - which he didn�t. "Fast forward to 2026 and Jade my girlfriend and I completed it on behalf of the Freeman Hospital and the Cardiology ward as just a small thank you to them for the everything they did for me and the support they gave to my family and mates during the time I was in hospital. Jamie said that so far he had raised just under �900. "Thank you so much to everyone that has donated on our just giving page. "It means so much to us that we will be able to give something back to Freeman hospital to say thank you."
